title: Add helpers for regression-vs-baseline alerts + maintenance-window suppression (perf-canary)
author: Tomáš Novák
description: Context: perf-canary is standardizing alert semantics for "regression vs baseline" across p95 latency and tokens/sec slices (model/region/gpu_sku/runtime_build). During rollout/backtesting we saw a few classes of false positives that were hard to suppress consistently: (1) deploy windows (runtime rollout, autoscaler rebalance) where baseline is shifting, (2) canary warmup/cache priming periods, and (3) maintenance windows / regional work where we should not page but still want signals for analysis. This PR adds small, opinionated helpers to slo-toolkit so perf-canary (and other services) can define regression alerts with consistent math, annotations, and suppression behavior. What changed: (a) new regression_vs_baseline() helper that takes: current series, baseline series, direction ("increase"/"decrease"), threshold as ratio and/or absolute delta, minimum sample guard (via a separate gate series), and optional "baseline_kind" (rolling vs pinned). The helper emits standardized labels/annotations used for grouping/dedup and for payload enrichment (baseline kind, baseline window, threshold). (b) new maintenance_window_suppress() helper that accepts a boolean series (or 0/1 gauge) indicating suppression state and wraps the alert expression so we still record the underlying regression in a separate "-suppressed" recording rule (optional) while preventing firing. (c) consistent deploy-window suppression primitive based on a "deploy_event" gauge; this is intentionally generic so perf-canary can wire it up to runtime deploy annotations without hardcoding runtime specifics into this library. Notes/decisions: We intentionally do not bake in model/region labels here; the caller remains responsible for controlling cardinality. We also keep all suppression logic opt-in; the default regression helper does not change alerting behavior unless you pass a suppression signal. Example usage is included in examples/perf_canary_regression_alerts.jsonnet to match the patterns in observability-pack PRs. Rollout: perf-canary will consume this helper in its alert rule definition update (tracked in ENG-2846/ENG-2848).

review_conversation: Sean Gallagher: The high-level direction is right. Two questions: (1) Can we ensure the helper sets a stable dedup key label so paging doesn’t explode when baseline kind changes? (2) For suppression, we should make sure we don’t lose visibility entirely; I’d prefer a recording rule to preserve the regression magnitude even when suppressed.

Tomáš Novák (author): Good call. Added `alert_dedup_key` annotation + optional `dedup_labels` passthrough (default includes alertname, service, region, model). For suppression, the helper now supports `record_suppressed=true` to emit a `:suppressed` recording rule for the raw regression ratio/delta (see updated example).

Allison Grant: Please align naming with observability standards: `baseline_window` vs `baseline_lookback`, and annotations should be consistent across alerts. Also, we should avoid adding any labels that increase cardinality by default.

Tomáš Novák (author): Updated to `baseline_lookback` and `baseline_kind` annotations, no new default labels beyond what caller provides. The helper only adds annotations; labels are caller-controlled. README updated with the standard set we expect perf-canary to use.
Nadia Rahman: Can you clarify the "increase" vs "decrease" semantics? For tokens/sec, the regression is a decrease, but the ratio math should still be intuitive in dashboards.

Tomáš Novák (author): Added docs + tests: for `direction="decrease"`, we compute `baseline/current` for ratio (so > 1.0 means worse), and for `direction="increase"` we compute `current/baseline`. This keeps 'ratio > threshold' consistent for alerting. Example updated with tokens/sec decrease using threshold_ratio=1.08 (8% worse).
Rafael Mendes: Request: include a standard annotation for runbook link and "suppressed_reason" when maintenance_window_suppress is active. Our incident-bot formatter can pick it up.

Tomáš Novák (author): Added optional params `runbook_url` and `suppressed_reason` to the wrapper; if suppressed, we attach `suppressed_reason` annotation and keep `runbook_url` on the alert definition. Example shows both.
Sean Gallagher: LGTM with the changes. Please make sure the default behavior is safe (no suppression unless explicitly wired).
Tomáš Novák (author): Confirmed. Suppression wrapper is separate; regression helper is pure expression generation. Default example is unsuppressed unless `maintenance_window` is provided.
Allison Grant: Approved. Thanks for keeping cardinality concerns in mind.
Rafael Mendes: Approved. This will make the pager payloads much more consistent.
release_notes: Internal: slo-toolkit now provides regression_vs_baseline() + maintenance_window_suppress() helpers for consistent perf regression alert semantics (used by perf-canary rollout).
